entities.summary: Aristokles (b. 600 BCE, Attica) was a renowned musician and composer of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Attica. He was a key figure in the development of Attican music, known for his innovative compositions and collaborations with prominent artists of the time. Aristokles' works have been extensively studied and performed in modern times, providing valuable insights into the artistic and cultural landscape of ancient Greece. His legacy extends to the wider Mediterranean region, where his music influenced the development of various art forms. The influence of Aristokles can be seen in the works of later Greek musicians, such as Alcibiades and Pheidias, who credited him with inspiring their own musical compositions. Aristokles' significance in the history of music is undeniable, as he helped shape the sound of ancient Greece and left a lasting impact on the development of Western classical music.
